wanted: 000: I wanted to know what the black thing was before it spoke. The fragment answers by taking a frame of me, and I wanted that kept as the price of every later answer.
010: I wanted P'taxx to have actually seen one of these before. He does. Good.
022: I wanted the lattice to make the three routes I did not take visible as cost, not as options.
040a-make: I wanted the choice to cost something I could name. It costs the copy's reclassification and my unmeasurability, and I could name both.
040a-1: I wanted the ledger to do something new to me. Instead it just... works. The scene tells me 'the finishing is the work' and I wanted a scene that made me feel the finishing instead.
040a-2: I wanted the unmaking to have a visible wound. The copy turning its head back to me was the only concrete beat; everything after it is explanation.
040b: I wanted to know what the citywide test actually asks of a random cat in the street. The scene says the question is wider but never shows one other cat being asked.
040c: I wanted the cistern's naming of me to come with a sound or a shape, not just letters on a wall. The kit replaying my flinch was the best beat in the whole Stray line.
040d-1: I wanted the dyer to refuse. She does, then signs. The two lines of dialogue carried the whole scene.
040e: I wanted to know why I would carry tomorrow's correction instead of tonight's. The net of a hundred paws gives me a reason that is also a threat. Good.
040e-1: I wanted the palace to answer the carrying. The door closing behind me was enough, but I wanted one more beat on the far side.
040e-2: I wanted the refusal to be witnessed by someone who would matter later. The dyer's 'They saw you stop' is that beat, and it lands.

050g-1: I wanted to see what the room does with a corrected name. The scene spends the scroll and holds the name open, which is the right state to leave, but the frontier note reads like a to-do list.
050g-2: I wanted the shoulder-width door to matter immediately. It does, but the scene ends before I feel the cost of leaving my own record behind.
feared: 022a: that the lattice filing was the end and the story would flatten into a room I had already been to.
040a-1: that the witness standing up was a trap that would make me the record permanently with no way out. It is that, and I wanted the scene to show the door closing in my face. It does not.
040c: that the cistern lid jamming meant the city below was coming up. The scene does not pay that fear off or drop it; it just moves on.
040e: that carrying the correction would make me the method's tool without my choosing it. The net beat shows exactly this and I feared it for three scenes.
attention_intensified: 022: the lattice's fourth point landing on the reliquary made me read the next line twice.
040a-make: 'I did not give it the angle of a look-away' was the first line in the whole walk where I felt like a player instead of a reader.
040d-1: the dyer's one blue line through the inherited name. Concrete, priced, irreversible. Best beat of the Stray line.
040e-2: 'They saw you stop.' The refusal leaf earns its existence in that single line.
050g-1: the seal breaking under the sheet's edge and never closing again. A durable trace I can carry forward.
attention_weakened: 022a: the mid-scene restatement of the lattice drop. I skimmed it because I had just been through it.
040a-1: the last four paragraphs are a chain of 'X is Y, Y is Z' abstractions. I lost the thread of what is actually happening to me as a character in the room.
040a-2: the same recursive abstraction chain appears here too, mirrored. Reading both leaves back to back felt like reading the same paragraph with one word swapped.
040e-1: the net-of-paws imagery is repeated from the parent scene 040e and I stopped seeing new information in it.
050g-2: the frontier note is dense and procedural. I had to re-read it to extract what I actually owe and what I actually know.
confused: 022: why does the lattice show me all three routes simultaneously if I already took P'taxx's? Is the temple point a thing that still happened, or a thing that could have? The scene does not say.
040a: the distinction between the copy, the subject, and the record blurred. I kept asking which one is standing up. The scene does not re-assert which is which before the fork.

040a-1 vs 040a-2: the two leaves describe nearly identical end states from slightly different angles. After reading both I could not tell you what I have, what I owe, or what is different in the room besides the copy's orientation.
040c: the cistern naming me — is the name spoken, written, shown to the kit, or all three? The scene says 'the cistern identified them' which is a summary, not a scene.
040e-1: on the far side of the palace door, what does the carrying feel like? The scene ends at the door and the frontier note carries the weight, but I wanted one beat of the net on the other side.
050g-1: the frontier note lists five open pressures. I could not tell which one the next scene would have to answer first.
residue: the held frame of the recoil in the black — the first time the story showed me what it was keeping.
the dyer's one blue line through a name that was never hers.
the dead sliver in its blue cloth: the only thing in the street that is not repeating.
'They saw you stop.' The refusal is a state the city now holds, not just a state I chose.
the shoulder-width door: a constraint that will not widen again, which I can feel in my paws before the next scene.
the withheld name itself: never spoken, never shown, always the thing the record is about. It works as pressure because the story refuses to spend it.
